# Birko.Security.OAuth.Server

## Overview
OAuth2 authorization server implementation. Pure handler library — no ASP.NET dependency. Hosts route HTTP requests to per-endpoint handler classes; persistence flows through `Birko.Data.Stores` so the same code runs against SQL, ElasticSearch, MongoDB, etc.

Companion to `Birko.Communication.OAuth` (client side). Both projects can be used in the same process — a service issuing tokens with this project and consuming tokens from upstream providers with the client.

## Project Location
`Birko.Security.OAuth.Server/`

## Structure
```
Birko.Security.OAuth.Server/
├── OAuthServer.cs                  — Composition root: owns one handler per endpoint
├── OAuthServerSettings.cs          — Lifetime + issuer config (extends Birko.Configuration.Settings)
├── OAuthErrorCodes.cs              — RFC 6749 §5.2 + RFC 8628 error codes
├── OAuthGrantTypes.cs              — grant_type / response_type constants, OAuthClientType enum
├── OAuthServerException.cs         — { ErrorCode, ErrorDescription, ErrorUri } envelope
├── Models/                         — AbstractModel descendants (persistable via Birko.Data.Stores)
│   ├── OAuthClient.cs              — registered client
│   ├── AuthorizationCode.cs        — one-shot code with PKCE challenge
│   ├── RefreshTokenRecord.cs       — hashed refresh token + revocation
│   ├── DeviceCodeRecord.cs         — RFC 8628 in-flight state
│   └── ConsentRecord.cs            — prior user consent per (client, scope)
│   └── Persistence/                — OAuthClientEntity, RefreshTokenEntity: the stored forms (lists/claims as JSON)
├── Stores/                         — IAsyncStore<T> subinterfaces with named lookups
│   ├── IOAuthClientStore.cs        — GetByClientIdAsync, GetByNameAsync
│   ├── IAuthorizationCodeStore.cs  — GetByCodeAsync, TryRedeemAsync (the single-use claim)
│   ├── IRefreshTokenStore.cs       — GetByHashAsync, TryRevokeAsync (rotation's claim), RevokeFamilyAsync
│   ├── IDeviceCodeStore.cs         — GetByDeviceCodeAsync / GetByUserCodeAsync
│   ├── IConsentStore.cs            — GetAsync(userId, clientId)
│   └── Factory/                    — the five stores over IStoreFactory (TASK-1013)
├── Extensions/
│   └── OAuthServerStoreFactoryServiceCollectionExtensions.cs — AddOAuthServerStores(IStoreFactory)
├── Endpoints/
│   ├── Token/                      — /token (all four grant types)
│   ├── Authorize/                  — /authorize (response_type=code only; OAuth 2.1 default)
│   ├── DeviceAuthorization/        — /device_authorization + Approve helper
│   └── ClientRegistration/         — RFC 7591 dynamic client registration
└── Internal/
    ├── PkceValidator.cs            — S256 + plain (fixed-time compare)
    ├── ClientSecretHasher.cs       — SHA-256 hex, fixed-time verify
    └── RandomStringGenerator.cs    — Base64Url + RFC 8628 user-code alphabet
```

## Dependencies
- `Birko.Configuration` — Settings hierarchy

- `Birko.Data.Core` — AbstractModel

## Stores over a store factory (TASK-1013)
`services.AddOAuthServerStores(StoreFactory.Create(backend, connectionString, p => …))` registers the five interfaces as
singletons over `IStoreFactory.GetAsyncStore<T>()` (`Stores/Factory/FactoryOAuthStores.cs`):
- `AuthorizationCode`, `DeviceCodeRecord`, `ConsentRecord` go through the factory's store as they are; they carry a
  DataAnnotations `[Table]` with the deleted SQLite package's names (`oauth_auth_codes`, `oauth_device_codes`,
  `oauth_consents`), which a SQL backend needs and which keeps that package's databases readable.
- `OAuthClient` and `RefreshTokenRecord` go through `Models/Persistence/OAuthClientEntity` / `RefreshTokenEntity`, the
  same shape on every backend: lists and claims as one JSON text column, everything else under its own name, the
  SQLite package's tables and columns. DataAnnotations attributes only, so this project does not reference
  Birko.Data.SQL; they declare no index (an existing table keeps its own; TASK-1023).
- A predicate over the model is rewritten to the entity by `ModelPredicateTranslator`; a predicate on a member kept in
  the JSON column (`RedirectUris`, `AllowedGrantTypes`, `AllowedScopes`, `Claims`) throws `NotSupportedException`
  naming it — never dropped, never evaluated in memory.
- `TryRedeemAsync` / `TryRevokeAsync` are `IAsyncConditionalUpdateStore<T>.UpdateIfAsync(guid, x => !x.Used, …)`, so
  of concurrent claims exactly one wins on every backend. `RevokeFamilyAsync` is one filtered `PropertyUpdate`.
- Construction (and `AddOAuthServerStores`) refuses, with `ArgumentException` naming the backend, a factory whose store
  does not implement `IAsyncConditionalUpdateStore<T>` (JSON, XML).
- Elasticsearch: its searches (every lookup, and `ReadAsync(guid)`) see a write only after an index refresh (~1 s), so
  every factory-store write calls `FactoryStoreSupport.MakeVisibleAsync`, which refreshes a store that implements
  `IAsyncRefreshableStore` (the user's choice over refusing Elasticsearch, TASK-1013). The contract runs every test on
  it, server flows included, with no refresh between the stores' own writes and reads.

Tests: `tests/Birko.Security.OAuth.Server.StoreFactory.Tests` (the shared contract, live on nine backends).

## Grant types supported
| Grant | Constant | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `client_credentials` | `OAuthGrantTypes.ClientCredentials` | Confidential clients only. No refresh per RFC 6749 §4.4.3. |
| `authorization_code` | `OAuthGrantTypes.AuthorizationCode` | PKCE enforced for public clients (`RequirePkceForPublicClients`, default true). |
| `refresh_token` | `OAuthGrantTypes.RefreshToken` | Refresh-token rotation enabled by default (`RotateRefreshTokens`, RFC 6819 §5.2.2.3). |
| `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code` | `OAuthGrantTypes.DeviceCode` | RFC 8628; poll-interval enforced as `slow_down`. |

`password` (resource-owner password) is intentionally **not** supported — deprecated by OAuth 2.1.

### Federated sign-in (TASK-517)

A subject who signed in elsewhere (GitHub, a corporate IdP) gets the server's own token pair from
`TokenEndpointHandler.IssueForSubjectAsync(clientId, subject, scope, claims)`. The pair behaves as if an authorization had
just completed, so the refresh token renews through the normal `refresh_token` grant, with rotation and reuse detection.

```csharp
var tokens = await oauthServer.Token.IssueForSubjectAsync(
    "web", "github:42", "read write",
    new Dictionary<string, string> { ["name"] = "octocat", ["roles"] = "admin" });
```

- The client must exist, be enabled and be allowed `refresh_token`. The scope is narrowed as for `client_credentials`.
- Extra claims are stored on `RefreshTokenRecord.Claims` and re-issued on every refresh, so a store must persist that
  property. A registered claim (`sub`, `client_id`, `iss`, `scope`, `aud`, `exp`, `iat`, `nbf`, `jti`) is refused.
- No client secret is checked: the host asserts the sign-in. Never expose it as an endpoint.

### Shaping a client_credentials token (TASK-520)

`TokenEndpointHandler.ShapeClientCredentialsToken` sets the subject and extra claims of a `client_credentials` access
token, after the client is authenticated and the scope granted. With it, an app does not replace the grant to name a
service account (DraCode's `ServiceAccountTokenIssuer` re-implemented client authentication, secret hashing and scope
narrowing for this alone).

```csharp
oauthServer.Token.ShapeClientCredentialsToken = (ctx, ct) =>
{
    ctx.Subject = $"service:{ctx.Client.Name}";
    ctx.Claims["name"] = ctx.Client.Name;
    return Task.CompletedTask;
};
```

The scope stays the grant's, space-delimited; read it as permissions with `ClaimMappingOptions.PermissionClaim = "scope"`
(Birko.Security.AspNetCore splits a `scope` claim on spaces). A registered claim, or an empty subject, throws
`InvalidOperationException`: it is a configuration error, not something to drop.

## Wire integration
The handlers don't know about HTTP. A host typically does:

```csharp
var server = new OAuthServer(settings, jwtProvider, tokenOptions,
    clientStore, codeStore, refreshStore, deviceStore, consentStore,
    deviceVerificationUri: "https://auth.example.com/device");

// /token endpoint (POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded)
app.MapPost("/token", async (HttpRequest req) =>
{
    var form = await req.ReadFormAsync();
    var request = new TokenRequest { GrantType = form["grant_type"], /* ... */ };
    try
    {
        var response = await server.Token.HandleAsync(request);
        return Results.Json(new { access_token = response.AccessToken, /* ... */ });
    }
    catch (OAuthServerException ex)
    {
        return Results.Json(TokenErrorResponse.From(ex), statusCode: 400);
    }
});
```

## Patterns
- Token endpoint dispatch is a `switch` on `grant_type` — each branch is `HandleXxxAsync(client, request, ct)` and any protocol violation throws `OAuthServerException(ErrorCodes.X, "…")`. The host maps the exception to RFC 6749 §5.2 JSON via `TokenErrorResponse.From(ex)`.
- `IAsyncStore<T>` is the only persistence contract — any backend that implements it works. Tests use `InMemoryStore<T>`.
  Shipped implementations: the factory stores here (`AddOAuthServerStores`, TASK-1013), and the companions
  `Birko.Security.OAuth.Server.InMemory` (the test double) and `.SqLite` (TASK-518; superseded, to be removed).
- Single use is claimed by the store: `TryRedeemAsync` (codes) and `TryRevokeAsync` (refresh rotation). Their default
  implementations are read-check-write (a race between concurrent requests, measured red 3/3 at TASK-518 through the
  old handler path); the shipped stores override them atomically. A lost rotation fails only that request (`invalid_grant`, no family
  revoke; decided by the user); a token read after its rotation committed is reuse and revokes the family.
- `OAuthClient.ClientType` is immutable post-creation. Changing public ↔ confidential would invalidate stored hash/PKCE assumptions.
- Stored secrets are SHA-256 hashed (not PBKDF2/bcrypt) — they're high-entropy random values issued by the server, so a per-request constant-time SHA-256 compare is sufficient. Verification uses `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`.
- Refresh tokens are stored as hashes too — the plaintext only exists transiently in `TokenResponse.RefreshToken` and in client memory.

## Maintenance

### README Updates
When making changes that affect the public API (handlers, settings, models, stores), update README.md.

### CLAUDE.md Updates
When adding new endpoints, grant types, or models, update this file to reflect the structure.

### Test Requirements
Every new public functionality must have corresponding unit tests in `Birko.Security.OAuth.Server.Tests` (xUnit + FluentAssertions). Each grant type must have at least: success path, expiry/invalid-grant path, and one client-misconfiguration path.
